# Floom

> A native Rust GUI library: self-drawn, retained-mode, GPU-accelerated, no browser
> dependency, fine-grained reactivity. Workspace "Floom 2.0": edition 2024, MSRV 1.91,
> version 0.2.0 (pre-1.0), MIT. The 1.0 bar is budgets and conformance suites, not a
> competitor feature count.

This file is the **fifteen-minute tier**: enough to open a window and change it.
The map is [docs/README.md](docs/README.md); the full tier is `docs/`.

## Fifteen minutes: a window that runs

```toml
# Cargo.toml
[package]
name = "hello"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[dependencies]
floom = { path = "path/to/floom/crates/app/floom", features = ["desktop", "renderer-gpu"] }
```

```rust
// src/main.rs
use floom::prelude::*;

fn main() {
    floom::run_desktop("Hello", Size::new(360.0, 240.0), |host| {
        let root = Stack::new(Axis::Vertical).gap(8.0).child(Child::new(
            ChildKey::index(0),
            LayoutRequest::new(),
            || Box::new(Button::new("Save")),
        ));
        host.mount_root(LayoutStyle::default(), root);
        host.frame();
    })
    .expect("a window");
}
```

`cargo run` opens a window with one button. Two facts about the manifest are the ones
people lose time to: `floom`'s `default` is `[]` (nothing is compiled in until asked),
and `run_desktop` needs **both** `desktop` and `renderer-gpu` — it drives the GPU
presenter. Three facts about the tree are worth knowing before you fight them:

- `build` runs **once**. Widgets are retained; you change them through
  `host.widget_mut::<T>(node)` from a callback, never by rebuilding the tree.
- `on_click(|| …)` handlers must be `'static`, so they cannot capture `host`. The
  bridge is `host.on_frame(|host| …)`: state changes in the handler, the tree is
  reconciled on the next frame.
- `host.frame()` paints the first frame; the platform drives the rest.

`floom create myapp --platforms ios` scaffolds the same tree with the
native hosts already wired (`floom package --platform ios|android` builds them).

## Quick facts for an agent

- Layout: `crates/{core,system,widgets,platform,render,native,devtools,frontend,app}`; the
  public facade is `crates/app/floom`. Design systems and the editor live under
  `crates/ecosystem/` in their own workspaces and are **not** part of the 1.0 surface.
- Tests that must keep compiling: `crates/app/floom/tests/{prelude_surface,feature_graph,docs_parity}.rs`.
  `docs_parity.rs` cross-checks `docs/examples.md` ↔ `examples/`,
  `docs/architecture.md` ↔ `scripts/check-architecture-deps.sh`, and every path named in
  `docs/release-policy.md` — moving a doc without updating its readers fails the build.
- Gates: `bash scripts/gate.sh` (or `just gate`). CI runs on GitHub
  (`github.com/ShuttleSpace/floom`, four workflows); the gate is still the authority for
  size, perf and the cross-target checks CI cannot reach.
- Tested targets (2026-11-24): `aarch64-apple-darwin`, `aarch64-apple-ios-sim`,
  `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` open a real window in CI — the
  desktop two with the software renderer. Everything else is device- or target-gated;
  `docs/release-policy.md` is the authority.
- There is no crates.io release yet, and `floom` **on crates.io is an unrelated project**.
  Depend on the path until the rename is decided.
- Agent protocol (`crates/system/floom-accuracy/src/agent/`): commands `Tree`, `Semantics`,
  `Scene`, `Screenshot`, `Performance`, `Schema`; actions `Tap`, `TypeText`, `Drag`.
  Selectors: `Key` (the author's `Child::named`), `Label`, `Role`, and `Id` (mount order —
  stable only while nothing mounts before it). Transports: in-process, and `127.0.0.1`
  only with a dev token. `crates/app/floom-mcp` exposes the same five tools over MCP; it
  attaches to a running app, it does not launch one.
- Component schema: `component_schema()` yields slots, properties (`style`/`layout`/`widget`
  with closed domains), events, tokens, and a runnable example per widget kind.
- Benchmarks: `scripts/check-perf-budgets.sh` (10% budgets against a single-machine
  baseline), `just gate size` (3 tiers), `scripts/gate.sh resources` (idle CPU, peak RSS,
  allocation counts, frame counts).
- TypeScript: `floom-tsx` generates Rust from TSX in-tree; there is **no** published npm
  package (`npm/@types-floom` is the in-repo type surface the generator is checked against).
